title: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting - Cultural and Creative Arts - Production of Patterns
exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: In art and design, a 'pattern' is best defined as:
options: A single, isolated image in the center of a page.
The systematic repetition of a motif or design unit over a surface.
A random splash of colors with no defined shapes.
The frame that holds a painting.
questions.explain: A pattern is created by repeating a basic unit or design (the motif) in a structured, organized manner across a surface, such as on fabric or wallpaper.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: When a single motif is repeated identically side-by-side and top-to-bottom on a regular, straight grid without shifting, the layout is known as a:
questions.explain: The simple repeat (or block repeat) is the most basic pattern layout where the motif is stacked directly above, below, and beside itself in a perfect grid.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Identify the type of pattern layout where every alternate vertical column is shifted down by half the height of the motif, causing the horizontal alignment to stagger.
questions.explain: In a half-drop repeat pattern, the design shifts downward by 50% in the next column, creating a staggered, diagonal visual flow rather than a rigid square grid.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: If a motif looks like it is facing its own reflection horizontally or vertically in the next grid, the pattern created is called a:
questions.explain: A mirror repeat pattern (or mirrored layout) flips the motif either left-to-right or top-to-bottom as it repeats, creating a reflected, symmetrical design.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: A pattern layout in which motifs are organized inside repetitive lozenge (rhombus) shapes rather than squares is known as a:
questions.explain: Diamond repeat patterns utilize a grid based on diamond (rhombus) shapes, laying the motifs out on intersecting diagonal axes.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Why is the production of repeat patterns critically important in the Nigerian textile industry (e.g., in making Ankara prints)?
options: It ensures the fabric is waterproof.
It allows a single small design to be printed continuously over many yards of fabric seamlessly.
It is a legal requirement to avoid paying taxes.
It stops the dyes from fading in sunlight.
questions.explain: Repeat patterns allow designers to create a seamless continuity. A printing roller with a single repeat unit can rotate and print endless yards of fabric without awkward breaks in the design.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: To manually produce an accurate simple repeat pattern on paper without redrawing the motif from scratch every time, a student can use:
options: Tracing paper or a cut-out stencil
questions.explain: Tracing paper or stencils allow the student to exactly copy (transfer) the initial motif repeatedly across the grid, ensuring uniform size and shape in every repetition.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: When producing a pattern design using the simple repeat method, how should the grid be drawn on the paper?
options: With perfectly measured, equally sized horizontal and vertical squares.
No grid should be used; the motifs are scattered blindly.
questions.explain: A simple repeat pattern relies on a precise, uniform grid of equal-sized blocks (usually squares) so the motif maintains its scale and perfect horizontal/vertical alignment.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
